look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Check an annual coarse squash vine or bush with alternate often deeply 5–7-lobed rough leaves. At stem nodes inspect stiff hairs and their swollen pustulate bases; on a mature fruit look for a firm, five-ribbed stalk. The staged image shows a cultivated straightneck squash plant, flowers and lobed leaves, NOT a stem-hair macro or a measured fruiting stalk.
taxonomy_notes: POWO/FNA accept Cucurbita pepo L. as a distinct species from C. melopepo. This approved source-pool record is a cultivated/escaped crop comparison; Texas introduced status in POWO does not certify an individual plant's origin. Preserve native-only metric exclusion.

morphology_keys.habit: Annual cultivated or escaped squash; sprawling vines or compact bush cultivars, variable growth form.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Alternate broad rough blades, often 5–7-lobed; cultivars vary in lobing, markings and size.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Large yellow unisexual flowers, with male and female flowers borne separately on same plant; female flower has swollen inferior ovary.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Very variable pepo fruit among pumpkin, zucchini and summer squash cultivars; fruiting peduncle often hard, five-angled/ribbed and not or gradually expanded at fruit.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Rough annual stems with commonly persistent hairs on strong pustulate bases; tendrils and nodes help separate from unrelated broad-leaved crops.

confused_with: Cucurbita melopepo (also annual; hair bases and fruit-stalk shape overlap; do not use pattypan fruit shape alone to resolve difficult cultivars)
Cucurbita foetidissima (perennial with mostly unlobed triangular leaves and smaller rounded gourds)
Cucumis melo (different genus; compare smaller flowers and fruiting stalk, nodes and tendrils)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Annual habit, coarse often lobed leaves, strongly pustulate-based stem hairs and five-ribbed fruiting stalk together support C. pepo; crop fruit color or shape is not reliable species-level evidence.
